title: The spectral norm on an algebraic extension of a complete nonarchimedean field
statement: Let $F$ be a complete field with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value $|\cdot|$, and let $L/F$ be an algebraic field extension, meaning that every $x\in L$ is a root of a nonzero polynomial over $F$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. For $x\in L$ let $p_x\in F[T]$ be its monic minimal polynomial (the monic polynomial of least degree vanishing at $x$), and put $d_x=\deg p_x$. Define $s(x)=\sup_{j\in\mathbf N}b_j(x)$, where $b_j(x)=|(p_x)_j|^{1/(d_x-j)}$ for $j<d_x$ and $b_j(x)=0$ otherwise; here $(p_x)_j$ is the coefficient of $T^j$. Then $s$ is a multiplicative nonarchimedean norm extending the absolute value of $F$: $s(x)=0$ exactly when $x=0$, $s(1)=1$, $s(x+y)\le\max(s(x),s(y))$, $s(xy)=s(x)s(y)$, and $s(cx)=|c|s(x)$ for $c\in F$. In particular the distance $s(x-y)$ and the given scalar action make $L$ a normed $F$-vector space. This $s(x)$ is Mathlib's $\operatorname{spectralNorm}_F(x)=\operatorname{spectralValue}(p_x)$.
